---
title: "Differential expression: many comparisons"
description: >
  Compare DE results across cell types, treatments, time points or assays:
  plot_multi_volcano(), plot_de_dots() and plot_fc_quadrant().
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_common.R")
```

**Question:** across several comparisons, how many genes change, which genes
change where, and do two comparisons agree?

| Function | Shows | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| `plot_multi_volcano()` | the genes of each comparison, one column each | the size and shape of each response |
| `plot_de_dots()` | chosen genes × comparisons: fold change and significance | specific genes across comparisons |
| `plot_fc_quadrant()` | fold changes of one comparison against another | whether two responses agree |

All three read their input with `standardize_de()` (see
[DE: one comparison](de-single.html)): a **named list** of DE tables (names
are the comparisons), or one long table with a comparison column
(`comparison.col`, e.g. `"cluster"` for `Seurat::FindAllMarkers()`).

As in the single-cell plots, the comparisons play the part of `group.by` (the
units compared, marked by their colour) and the optional `groups` of
comparisons (e.g. a lineage above its cell types) that of `split.by`: blocks
marked by a bar and a name, black by default (`groups.cols`), opposite the
comparison names (`groups.side`).

**Data:** interferon-β (IFN-β) vs control in each cell type of the PBMCs of
[Kang et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4042): counts summed per donor,
condition and cell type (pseudobulk), edgeR quasi-likelihood test paired by
donor, for the 6 cell types with at least 10 cells in every sample. Testing
samples rather than cells avoids the inflated p-values of per-cell tests,
which treat cells as replicates.

```{r data}
de <- docs_kang_de()
names(de)
# DE genes per cell type
vapply(de, function(t) sum(t$FDR < 0.05), integer(1))
```

## Multi-comparison volcano

One column per comparison, marked by a strip of its colour and its name on
top: genes at their log2 fold change, spread by their density, the
non-significant ones in grey; the cutoffs (±`logfc.cutoff`, default 1) as
dashed lines; counts of up- and down-regulated genes above and below.

```{r multi}
plot_multi_volcano(de)
```

CD14 monocytes respond with the most genes; the top genes of every cell type
include interferon-stimulated genes. Colour is the −log10 adjusted p-value
(warm for up, cool for down), saturating at the 95th percentile of the DE
genes; each side of the colour bar ends at its own most significant gene, so
the direction with weaker p-values is not faded.

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `groups`

A second level: comparisons of a group are drawn together, the group marked
by a bar and its name at the bottom (`groups.side = "labels"` puts it at the
top, beyond the comparison names).

```{r multi-groups}
lineage <- c(
    "CD4 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD8 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "NK" = "Lymphoid",
    "B" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD14 Mono" = "Myeloid",
    "FCGR3A Mono" = "Myeloid"
)
plot_multi_volcano(de, groups = lineage)
```

#### `flip`

Comparisons as rows: down-regulated genes on the left, up-regulated on the
right, the comparison names and strips on the left. `comparison.cols` takes a
palette name, or colours named by comparison (e.g. the cell type colours of
the embedding plots):

```{r multi-flip}
plot_multi_volcano(
    de,
    flip = TRUE,
    groups = lineage,
    comparison.cols = "okabe-ito",
    label.n = 2
)
```

#### `layout`

`"pvalue"` places genes across their column by −log10 adjusted p-value (each
column is a sideways volcano); `"jitter"` spreads them uniformly.

```{r multi-layout}
plot_multi_volcano(de, layout = "pvalue")
```

#### `color.by`

`"sharing"` colours genes by the number of comparisons they are DE in:
responses shared by all cell types versus specific to one. `"direction"`
uses one colour per direction.

```{r multi-sharing}
plot_multi_volcano(de, color.by = "sharing", label = "none")
```

#### `order`

`"n_de"` puts the comparisons with the most DE genes first; `"cluster"`
groups comparisons with similar fold-change profiles.

```{r multi-order}
plot_multi_volcano(de, order = "cluster", label.n = 2)
```

#### Cutoffs and `show.ns`

A lower `logfc.cutoff`, and only the DE genes (`show.ns = FALSE`):

```{r multi-ns}
plot_multi_volcano(
    de,
    show.ns = FALSE,
    logfc.cutoff = 0.5,
    label = "none"
)
```

## DE dot plot

Chosen genes across comparisons: colour is the log2 fold change, size the
−log10 adjusted p-value, and non-significant results are faded. Each
comparison is marked by a coloured dot, as the groups of the single-cell dot
plot (`comparison.marker = "dot"`, `"strip"` or `"none"`). Without
`features`, the top `n` genes of each comparison:

```{r dots}
plot_de_dots(de, n = 3)
```

The colour scale is centred on 0 and runs from the most negative to the most
positive fold change of the significant dots, each side to its own full
colour; give `logfc.limits` to share one scale between figures.

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Gene groups

A named list of genes draws groups of columns, marked by bars on top
(coloured with `feature.group.cols`):

```{r dots-features}
genes <- list(
    "Interferon-stimulated" = c("ISG15", "IFI6", "IFIT1", "IFIT3", "MX1", "OAS1"),
    "Chemokines" = c("CXCL10", "CCL2", "CCL8")
)
plot_de_dots(de, features = genes)
```

#### `significance`

`"grey"` draws non-significant results grey; `"hide"` leaves them out:

```{r dots-grey}
plot_de_dots(de, features = genes, significance = "grey")
```

#### Clustering and `flip`

Genes and comparisons ordered by clustering of their fold changes; genes as
rows, comparisons as columns marked by colour strips:

```{r dots-cluster}
plot_de_dots(
    de,
    n = 4,
    cluster.features = TRUE,
    cluster.comparisons = TRUE,
    flip = TRUE,
    comparison.marker = "strip"
)
```

#### `groups`

Comparisons in groups of rows, each marked by a bar and its name (here in
colour, beyond the comparison names):

```{r dots-groups}
plot_de_dots(
    de,
    features = genes,
    groups = lineage,
    groups.cols = c(Lymphoid = "#2C5DA8", Myeloid = "#B5338A"),
    groups.side = "labels"
)
```

## Quadrant plot

The fold changes of two comparisons against each other, coloured by where
each gene is significant; counts of genes significant in both in each
quadrant, and the correlation of the fold changes above the panel. Do
monocytes and B cells respond to IFN-β with the same genes?

```{r quadrant}
plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    label.n = 3
)
```

Most genes changed in both change in the same direction (concordant,
top-right and bottom-left), and B cells respond to fewer genes, more weakly
(the cloud lies below the diagonal on the right).

### Variants {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### `trend`

A least-squares line with its 95% confidence band, fitted on the genes of
the correlation (`cor.on`). Both fold changes are noisy estimates, which
biases a least-squares slope toward 0 (regression dilution): the line shows
the trend, but its slope is not the ratio of the two responses.

```{r quadrant-trend}
plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    cor.on = "significant",
    trend = TRUE,
    label = "none"
)
```

#### Two treatments

The comparisons can come from different experiments, tools or designs. Here,
macrophages ([Alasoo et al. 2018](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41588-018-0046-7))
stimulated with IFN-γ or infected with *Salmonella*, each against naive,
paired by donor:

```{r quadrant-mac}
mac <- docs_macrophage()
counts <- filter_low_expression_genes(mac$counts, min_group_size = 6)
y <- edgeR::normLibSizes(edgeR::DGEList(counts))
design <- model.matrix(~ donor + condition, data = mac$samples)
fit <- edgeR::glmQLFit(y, design)
test_ifng <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "conditionIFNg")
test_sl1344 <- edgeR::glmQLFTest(fit, coef = "conditionSL1344")
de_ifng <- edgeR::topTags(test_ifng, n = Inf)
de_sl1344 <- edgeR::topTags(test_sl1344, n = Inf)
plot_fc_quadrant(
    de_ifng,
    de_sl1344,
    name.x = "IFN-γ",
    name.y = "Salmonella",
    logfc.cutoff = 1
)
```

#### `categories` and `cor.on`

Colour only genes significant in both; correlation of the genes significant
in either comparison:

```{r quadrant-both}
plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["CD4 T"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "CD4 T",
    categories = "both",
    cor.on = "significant",
    correlation = "pearson"
)
```

#### `label = "selected"`

```{r quadrant-selected}
plot_fc_quadrant(
    de[["CD14 Mono"]],
    de[["B"]],
    name.x = "CD14 Mono",
    name.y = "B",
    label = "selected",
    label.features = c("ISG15", "CXCL10", "IFIT1", "MX1")
)
```

#### Peaks to genes: `map.y`

To compare RNA with chromatin (ATAC, ChIP, CUT&RUN), map the peaks of `de.y`
to genes with `map.y` (e.g. from a ChIPseeker annotation); with several peaks
per gene, the most significant one is used (`map.summary`). The peak table
below is **simulated** from the monocyte RNA fold changes, only to show the
input format:

```{r quadrant-peaks}
rna <- de[["CD14 Mono"]]
set.seed(1)
genes_with_peaks <- sample(rownames(rna), 3000)
n_peaks <- sample(1:3, length(genes_with_peaks), replace = TRUE)
peak_gene <- rep(genes_with_peaks, n_peaks)
peak_logfc <- 0.5 * rna[peak_gene, "logFC"] + rnorm(length(peak_gene), sd = 0.6)
peaks <- data.frame(
    logFC = peak_logfc,
    row.names = paste0("peak_", seq_along(peak_gene))
)
peaks$PValue <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(peaks$logFC) / 0.4)
peaks$FDR <- p.adjust(peaks$PValue, "BH")
peak_to_gene <- data.frame(peak = rownames(peaks), gene = peak_gene)
head(peak_to_gene, 3)

plot_fc_quadrant(
    rna,
    peaks,
    name.x = "RNA",
    name.y = "ATAC (simulated)",
    map.y = peak_to_gene
)
```
